title: Use the layer-to-default-action map for route sequences

facts.note: Task text mentions route sequences or the layer/action mapping.
Whether a route-sequence step is attached to one of these layers is read from the sequence text; no dedicated observer exists.

fires: A route sequence is being defined and a step for the presentation, application, domain or integration layer needs its default action.
A default action is being selected for a layer in a route sequence.
An existing route sequence's layer defaults are being checked or revised.
doesNotFire: Work that involves no route sequence and no layer-to-action mapping.
Edits to a sequence that change neither a step's layer nor its action (for example, prose wording fixes).

given: A route sequence has steps assigned to the presentation, application, domain or integration layer
when: You define, select or check the default action for a layer in that sequence
then: Use the layer's default action: presentation → command, application → use_case, domain → validate, integration → persist.
prefer: Write steps as <layer>.<default action>: presentation.command, application.use_case, domain.validate, integration.persist.
avoid: Giving a layer a different default action than the map, for example making persist the domain default or validate the presentation default.
why: With one fixed layer-to-default-action map, every route sequence uses the same defaults, so sequences stay consistent and predictable.
evidence: Any default action stated or used for presentation, application, domain or integration in the route sequence matches the map: command, use_case, validate, persist.
verifier_detail: Term layer_action: 'layer -> default action.' values: presentation=command, application=use_case, domain=validate, integration=persist. Compare each layer's stated or applied default action with this map. This is a default mapping: the source does not say that a non-default action on a step is forbidden, so do not flag one as a violation of this rule.

Restates the source's own notation (presentation.command, etc.) as a concrete move. It sets no order for the steps.

additions.text: Giving a layer a different default action than the map.
additions.justification: The negative form of the source map. It concerns what the default is, not a ban on non-default actions.

additions.text: Consistency and predictability from one fixed map.
additions.justification: The source gives no explicit reason. This is the minimal reason implied by having a single shared default map.

additions.justification: Stops verifiers from turning a default mapping into a universal requirement, which goes beyond the source.
